output.title: Tablet blister packing into 10-up strips

product.name: Tablet blister strips (10 cavities)
product.description: Blister strip made from PVC cavities, filled with tablets, sealed with aluminium lid foil, then cut into individual strips. Each finished strip is 95 × 45 mm (flat blister size) and goes into folding carton with a leaflet; quality rejects strips with any empty cavity.

steps.name: FormBlisterCavities
steps.does: Heat-form PVC film to create blister cavities for one 10-cavity strip.

steps.name: DoseTablets
steps.does: Drop/dose tablets into each blister cavity.

steps.name: InspectCavities
steps.does: Use a camera to check every cavity is filled; identify strips containing any empty cavity.

steps.name: SealLidFoil
steps.does: Heat-seal aluminium lid foil over the blister cavities.

steps.name: CutBlisterStrips
steps.does: Cut/trim the sealed web into individual strips (separate the strips apart).

steps.name: PackIntoCartons
steps.does: Place two finished strips into a folding carton and add the leaflet.

output.quality: Strips with at least one empty blister cavity are rejected (discarded or diverted to a reject bin) and do not proceed to cartoning.
constraints: GMP clean room required (controlled environment, wipe-down/cleaning practices, restrict airborne contamination).
Finished blister strips are formed from PVC film and sealed with aluminium lid foil.
Strip size is 95 × 45 mm; blister cavities must be 10 per strip (owner statement).
Rejected product: any strip with an empty cavity is removed before cartoning.
assumptions: A “finished unit” for throughput is one individual blister strip (not the folding carton).
A folding carton contains exactly 2 blister strips plus 1 leaflet (as stated).
The line runs in steady-state; changeover time is ignored for the per-hour target.
Blister height (the third dimension for the model) is assumed ~10 mm because it was not provided.
Reject handling is purely diversion/discard (no rework).
Tablet type/form factor (shape, count per cavity, presence of chamfers, tablet thickness) is not modeled explicitly; it is treated as a discrete part dispensed into cavities.

questions.question: Do you have the blister “stack height” (typical finished blister thickness including lid foil) and exact cavity pitch/row pattern (how the 10 cavities are laid out)? This affects forming/sealing/vision fixturing.
questions.why: The twin needs correct cavity geometry to size stations and inspection coverage.

questions.question: Is the 60 strips/min steady with no planned downtime, and is it measured at “finished strips exiting cartoning” (after carton insertion), or earlier (after cutting)?
questions.why: This determines whether the bottleneck is packaging or earlier thermoforming/sealing.

questions.question: What are the folding-carton handling details: are cartons pre-erected or erected on the line, and is carton closing (taping/gluing) manual or machine? Also, how is the leaflet inserted (drop-in and then close)?
questions.why: Cartoning station design and takt depend on erect/close method and leaflet insertion time.
